content:
The new (still in construction) website is now available at: https://google-deepmind.github.io/formal-conjectures/ !

Feedback and suggestions are welcome:)
We are planning to include the informal docstrings including links to original problems next...
It would be great to get this working with verso, especially now that verso has a manual!

Looks great for a first version. Some initial observations:

Should this be Results or Problems? I feel like Problems would be more fitting...

Also the formatting on the About / Contribute Sites looks a bit off.

Yeah "Problems" is probably better than "Results" here.
About formatting looking off: suggestion for improvement/ pull request are most welcome this wasn't exhaustively tested (for instance, I didn't yet look at it on a phone)

experimenting with verso integration here:
https://mo271.github.io/formal-conjectures/

This builds some verso facets to /src/ and then extracts the module docstring, the theorem docstring and the theorem statement from that.
(still has some rough edges)

out of the box verso was failing on some of our files in Util (which are not the focus of the website, so I ignored the failures for now), but perhaps good to investigate if this is already fixed in verso at head (we are lagging behind running v4.27)
It looks a bit weird that you're claiming 19 formalisations of millennium problems when there are only seven problems
This is meant to be problems related to the millennium problems (e.g special cases), but this is indeed worth clarifying on the website!

Maybe it might make sense to count problems on a file basis, but this would also be a bit understating in some cases... for example the Riemann File contains Problems, which would be indeed considered different e.g. RH, GRH, ERH but they are just not all a Millenium Problems...

yeah, perhaps we should also exclude in the counts test statements like https://google-deepmind.github.io/formal-conjectures/theorem/?name=ExtendedRiemannHypothesis.extended_riemann_hypothesis_dedekindZeta_of_isInCriticalStrip
Currently the count just means there are this number of theorems the Millennium Prize Problems subdirectory

I just looked around a bit on the website, the main page, and the theorem and browse pages look really good and clean! I have some issues with the src pages, e.g. this one

  • I cannot scroll the source file of the screen (if I make my window very small, I can scroll horizontally, but not vertically). This happens in both Firefox and Chrome for me.
  • Three links near the top (Skip to Content, FormalConjectures, Wikipedia) lead to 404s.

Thanks for the bug report, we should look into this. Also the weird way Verso renders the comments for theorems, with the lines beginning and ending the comments is something that I have to mean to make more pretty

Quick little PR to fix the scroll issue: https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/5234

I'll take a look at the broken links when I get a chance.
